skill.name: diffdock
skill.description: DiffDock workflow guidance for protein-ligand docking, virtual screening, batch input preparation, confidence review, and result analysis.
skill.summary: Guide DiffDock protein-ligand docking workflows from input setup to confidence-based result review.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Molecular docking workflows need careful setup, batch inputs, and clear confidence interpretation. This skill guides DiffDock runs, validation, analysis, and result review.
actual_capabilities: Guide single protein-ligand DiffDock runs from PDB, sequence, SMILES, SDF, or MOL2 inputs.
Prepare and validate batch CSV files with the included helper script.
Explain DiffDock confidence score ranges and when to validate poses carefully.
Show virtual screening, ensemble docking, and downstream rescoring workflows.
Check local DiffDock dependencies, CUDA status, RDKit, PyTorch Geometric, and model files.
Summarize DiffDock confidence results and export ranked CSV reports.
limitations: It does not predict binding affinity by itself.
It requires a working DiffDock installation and a compatible GPU for practical speed.
It is not designed for protein-protein, covalent, or large peptide docking.
Predicted poses need expert review and experimental validation before decisions.

use_cases.title: Dock a Lead Compound
use_cases.description: Run a single protein-ligand docking workflow and review the top predicted binding poses.

use_cases.title: Screen a Compound Library
use_cases.description: Prepare batch CSV inputs, run many complexes, and rank predictions by confidence.

use_cases.title: Validate Docking Setup
use_cases.description: Check dependencies, CUDA support, model files, and expected DiffDock output structure.

prompt_templates.title: Plan One Docking Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me dock one ligand to one protein with DiffDock. I have a PDB file and a SMILES string. List the required inputs, recommended settings, and result checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Batch Docking
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DiffDock batch workflow for these protein-ligand pairs. Include CSV validation steps, output organization, and confidence score review.

prompt_templates.title: Review Low Confidence Results
prompt_templates.prompt: My DiffDock results have low confidence scores. Diagnose likely causes and suggest parameter, protein preparation, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Screening Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a virtual screening pipeline with DiffDock, protein embedding reuse, confidence ranking, pose inspection, and downstream rescoring.

output_examples.input: Dock aspirin to a prepared protein structure and explain the expected outputs.
output_examples.output: A step plan covering input validation, a single DiffDock run, generated pose files, confidence score interpretation, and visual inspection guidance.

output_examples.input: Prepare a batch docking campaign for 200 ligands against one target protein.
output_examples.output: A workflow for batch CSV creation, ligand validation, GPU batch sizing, embedding reuse, confidence ranking, and CSV export of top poses.

output_examples.input: Explain whether high DiffDock confidence means strong binding.
output_examples.output: A clear explanation that confidence measures pose certainty, not affinity, with recommendations for rescoring and experimental validation.

best_practices: Validate protein files, ligand formats, and batch CSV columns before running large jobs.
Use multiple samples and inspect top poses instead of relying on one ranked output.
Combine DiffDock confidence with rescoring, structural review, and experimental validation.
anti_patterns: Treating DiffDock confidence scores as binding affinity values.
Running large screens on CPU without checking performance limits.
Using unprepared protein structures or invalid ligand files without validation.

faq.question: Does this skill predict binding affinity?
faq.answer: No. It helps predict binding poses and interpret confidence, but affinity needs separate scoring or experiments.

faq.question: Can I use protein sequences instead of PDB files?
faq.answer: Yes. DiffDock can use protein sequences through ESMFold, but this adds time and model uncertainty.

faq.question: What ligand formats are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers SMILES strings and common structure files such as SDF and MOL2.

faq.question: Is a GPU required?
faq.answer: A GPU is strongly recommended. CPU runs can be much slower and are poor for large batches.

faq.question: How should I use confidence scores?
faq.answer: Use them for initial pose ranking and triage. Confirm results with visualization, rescoring, and domain review.

faq.question: Can this handle virtual screening?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes batch CSV preparation, protein embedding reuse, confidence ranking, and export workflows.
